summary: Repetitive pitch: line 3 says 'nothing leaves your machine' and line 5 repeats 'fully offline, no cloud' — same concept twice in three lines.
suggested_fix: Merge into one crisp sentence, e.g.: 'VoiceFlow turns your voice into text using a local Whisper model — fully offline, available as a cross-platform desktop app (Tauri + Rust), native macOS app (Swift 6 · XcodeGen), and a browser-based demo (WebAssembly).'

summary: Feature bullet descriptions explain obvious outcomes of named features, adding word count without new information (e.g., 'Auto-copy to clipboard — optionally paste the transcript into the frontmost app').
suggested_fix: Shorten each description to the essential detail only. Example: replace 'Auto-copy to clipboard — optionally paste the transcript into the frontmost app' with 'Auto-copy to clipboard'; replace 'Streaming transcription — real-time partial transcripts via Groq API (optional, free tier)' with 'Streaming transcription (Groq API, optional)'. Keep only details that aren't self-evident.

summary: Windows section has verbose explanatory comments telling users what they should already know ('Install Rust (if not installed)', 'Download from: ...', 'Select
suggested_fix: Trim to bare commands and links; remove meta-commentary that restates the obvious or duplicates the linked page's own instructions.

summary: The manual setup path repeats work the one-line scripts do, but with extra inline comments explaining what each command does ('Download the Whisper model (141MB)'). Readers who can read a script don't need line-by-line commentary.
suggested_fix: Keep only the one-line script paths and note the manual path once as an alternative. Remove the curl comment explaining the file size and URL purpose; the command itself is self-explanatory.

summary: Last sentence re-states a prerequisite that was already covered in the 'macOS' and 'One-Time Setup' sections.
suggested_fix: Delete the sentence entirely — the build tool requirements belong in the prerequisites section, not buried after the Xcode steps.

summary: 'What it does' section restates features already covered in the feature list (lines 21–29), just phrased differently.
suggested_fix: Replace with a short note that this section is about the streaming mode's unique value-add (sub-second latency, smart editing on-the-fly) without re-listing general product features.

summary: 'pure offline dictation page that runs Whisper tiny.en entirely in the browser via WebAssembly — no backend, no API key' repeats the same 'no cloud / no API key' pitch already made in line 3.
suggested_fix: Shorten to: 'A fully offline browser-based dictation page using the tiny.en Whisper model via WASM — no backend or API key needed.'

summary: Privacy section includes 'Open your browser's Network tab and dictate — you'll see zero requests in default mode.' This is hand-holding instruction for something most technically-literate readers will verify themselves.
suggested_fix: Delete that sentence; the bullet above it already states 'Zero network requests. All processing happens on your device.'

summary: Project structure tree is extremely granular — nearly every individual source file is listed with a one-line comment, most of which restate what the filename already conveys (e.g., 'AppSettings.swift — Persisted settings', 'ModelManager.swift — Model download & caching').
suggested_fix: Collapse to directory-level listings with brief per-directory descriptions instead of per-file annotations. Keep the structure informative but remove comment-text that duplicates the filename's meaning.

summary: The 'Built for Kenneth Aman' footer is personal metadata that doesn't help a reader understand or use the project.
suggested_fix: Remove unless this is intentionally part of the project branding.
